clue.text: The carpenter is leaving a book

definitions.meaning: Chips is the traditional nickname for a carpenter, so this is a farewell said to a departing woodworker
the 1934 novella by James Hilton about a schoolmaster, later filmed

explanation.surface: A notice that the workshop's woodworker is off, and something to read.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips is the old nickname for a carpenter, especially a ship's carpenter, so the farewell to him is also the title of James Hilton's novel about a beloved teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of James Hilton's novel about the schoolmaster Mr Chipping, read literally, is a farewell.

clue.text: Farmland planted by Lord is best place to live

parts.note: the Lord is God
seed that is planted has been sown
country can mean rural land, the countryside

explanation.surface: Fields that a lord has seeded turn out to be the ideal home.
explanation.walkthrough: Land 'planted by Lord' is land sown by God, so the pieces run GOD, SOWN, then the farmland; 'by' only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an ideal region, praised as blessed by heaven above all others.

clue.text: Pub lacking in new feature — one may be standing

indicators.note: the new feature is shown without the pub, so those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: an innovation is a new feature
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A refurbished pub without the latest attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the standing kind: the applause an audience gives on its feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic applause from an audience is often given standing, so this is something that may be standing.

clue.text: Audible signal on end of satellite dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the bell comes first

parts.note: a bell rings as an audible signal

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word satellite

explanation.surface: A beep from a satellite dish signalling its reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like the satellite dish but it is the definition: an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for a good-looking person, and a belle is a beautiful woman.

clue.text: Cut up after head of panel replaced by English singer's wife

indicators.note: after places the cut-up word behind the altered panel
head of points to the first letter of the jury, which is the one swapped
replaced by says that first letter gives way to the English abbreviation

parts.note: a jury is a panel of people judging a case
to cut food up into cubes is to dice it

explanation.surface: Instructions for chopping something after a judging panel's chair is swapped for an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is Orpheus of Greek myth, who sang so well he nearly won his wife back from the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the wife of Orpheus, the legendary singer and lyre player.

clue.text: Regretting eating too many bitter herbs?

definitions.meaning: feeling sorry or remorseful about something
rue is a bitter herb, so someone full of it after overeating would be stuffed with rue

explanation.walkthrough: Rue is both regret and a bitter herb, so being full of rue reads as having eaten too much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry for what they did feels and looks sorrowful, full of rue in its old sense of regret.

clue.text: Shock speaking opportunity for stars

indicators.note: speaking says the word for shock is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: horror is shock
scope is room or opportunity

explanation.surface: A startling chance to speak, offered to celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like famous people but it is the newspaper astrology column, which is popularly called 'the stars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper readers checking their stars are reading an astrological forecast based on birth signs.

clue.text: Piped music starts to play in bar, receiving exclamation from Scotsman

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: A tune begins in a pub, greeted by a cry from a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' looks like a container signal but here it gives only its first letter, like 'play', 'in' and 'bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classical form of Highland bagpipe music with a theme and variations.

clue.text: Office has grip on power over administrative district

parts.note: a vice is a tool that grips
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
in British India a residency was an administrative district run by a resident

explanation.surface: A government office controls power over a local district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has', 'on' and 'over' only link the pieces in order; 'grip' is a noun for the tool, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The deputy president's post is an office of state, a position held.

clue.text: Fail to inhibit one fitter's reckless charm

I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.walkthrough: 'fitter' looks like a tradesman but is the comparative of fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means devilry or sorcery, a wild and reckless magic associated with devils.

clue.text: Legal scholar's right to books in excellent binding

explanation.surface: A law student is entitled to finely bound volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as letters, is AI; 'binding' plays on bookbinding.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a teacher and scholar of Jewish law, so a legal scholar fits.

clue.text: Girl has to survive on nothing

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to live is to survive

explanation.surface: A girl must get by with no money.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's given name, so it stands for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: Daughter hurried to collect carpets in shop

rugs are small carpets

explanation.definitionFit: In American usage this is a pharmacy that also sells everyday goods, a kind of shop.

clue.text: Sort of pan, new, with thin handle?

parts.note: something held on a stick has a thin handle

explanation.surface: A frying pan, brand new, with a slender handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that being on a stick is a stretch for having a thin handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A coated pan that food does not cling to is a common kind of frying pan.

clue.text: As we eat in, cooking Chinese

indicators.note: cooking turns these letters into something new, as raw ingredients become a dish

explanation.surface: Since we are dining at home, a Chinese meal is on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges AS WE EAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Taiwan, the Republic of China, are Chinese in a broad sense of nationality and culture.

clue.text: Nature so-called is alien to Man at first

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word Man

parts.note: other means foreign or alien

explanation.surface: The so-called natural world seems foreign to humankind's origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' signals that the definition is half of a phrase: the full name is Mother Nature.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural world is personified in the fixed phrase Mother Nature, so Nature is so called with this title.

clue.text: One missing a busy type that's made to go inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for made to go within the busy creature

parts.note: a busy bee is the type of worker always busy
sent means made to go

explanation.surface: Someone absent from a busy person who has been forced to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is away when expected, as from school or work, is absent.

clue.text: How one hopes to go from gym: in clothes

definitions.text: How one hopes to go from gym
definitions.meaning: a gym-goer hopes to leave the gym in good shape, healthy
a set of clothes worn together

explanation.surface: A gym-goer's hope of leaving trim, dressed in a new set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words: out, and fit after exercise; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of garments worn together is a costume or ensemble.

clue.text: Where Friar keeps supplementary rations?

explanation.definitionFit: A boarding-school pupil's container for extra food from home is the friar's namesake box.

clue.text: Acts as member of royal corps, making notes

definitions.text: Acts as member of royal corps
definitions.meaning: the Royal Observer Corps was a British civilian body that watched for enemy aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Observer Corps was a British volunteer organisation spotting aircraft; its members watch the skies. 'making' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who notices or remarks on something sees it and comments, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Strong criticism from three people left to carry bomb

parts.note: the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI
a trio is three people

explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' only links: the trio and left follow the bomb in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sulphuric acid, the word is used for bitterly caustic criticism or abuse.

clue.text: Pedalling endlessly over one strip of beach

clue.text: Spill entire can that's full of juice

clue.text: Creature caught in huge netting
